name: Creality Falcon A1C 10W
tagline: Class 1 enclosed mini diode with autofocus: a safe first laser for small gifts and coasters
tldr: The Falcon A1C 10W is Creality's smallest enclosed laser: a 150 × 150 mm bed in a fully closed Class 1 box with a motorized lifting platform and auto-focus. It engraves cork, bamboo, slate, leather and plywood cleanly and cut 5 mm plywood in one pass in a hands-on test, barely. Small bed and plastic build are the trade-offs for the price.
mainObjective: Safe, enclosed small-item engraving at home with light cutting on thin wood

priceRange.note: $369 basic, $399 with AI camera on Creality's store (Oct 2026); launch price was $299

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

cut: Basswood & plywood up to ~5 mm (one slow pass in testing)
cannot: Bare metal without the IR module

pros: Fully enclosed Class 1 box with lid interlock, flame detection, tilt sensor and USB safety key at an entry price
Motorized lifting bed and auto-focus: objects up to 148 mm tall without manual focus gauges
Arrives assembled: a hands-on reviewer was engraving on day one
Tool-free module swap: add the 1.2W IR head later for stainless, slate and black marble
cons: 150 × 150 mm bed: coasters, tags and small boards only
Plastic build reflects the price; Wi-Fi is 2.4 GHz only and camera setup needs the phone app
Auto-focus must be run before each job and the software lets you start without it
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 10W SKU of the Falcon A1C. Compare it with the 5W: pick the 10W if you want to cut thin plywood or engrave faster; the enclosure, bed and software are identical. The AI camera version costs about $30 more and cannot be added later.
proTips: Run the auto-focus before every job: the software does not force it. Use the presets as a starting point and test power on scrap, bamboo especially burns deeper than expected. For 5 mm plywood, slow down (around 300 mm/min at high power) and expect little margin.

faq.question: Can the Falcon A1C cut wood?
faq.answer: Thin wood, yes. Creality does not publish a cutting figure, but a hands-on review cut 5 mm plywood in one pass with the 10W module at 90% power and 300 mm/min, with little margin. Treat 3 mm as comfortable and 5 mm as the limit.

faq.question: Is the AI camera worth the extra cost?
faq.answer: If you engrave on existing objects (coasters, wallets, tags), yes: it makes placement much easier for about $30 more. It cannot be retrofitted to the basic version, so decide at purchase.

faq.question: Can I upgrade from 5W to 10W later?
faq.answer: Yes. Creality sells the 10W diode module separately and the swap is tool-free. The optional 1.2W infrared module uses the same mount.

faq.question: Can it engrave metal?
faq.answer: Coated metal with the diode, yes. For bare stainless steel, add the 1.2W IR (1064 nm) module: in testing it produced a clean dark mark on brushed stainless, slowly.

accessories.note: AI camera version only: cannot be added after purchase
Sold in Creality's Home Clean Kit bundles

moduleSystem.headline: Tool-free laser modules on the same A1C enclosure
moduleSystem.description: The Falcon A1C ships with a 5W or 10W diode module. Creality sells the 10W diode and a 1.2W 1064 nm infrared module separately; both clip onto the same head mount without tools. You run one module at a time: this is not a hybrid dual-source machine.

editorialDepth.advantages: The 10W A1C is the version to buy if you want the enclosure for safety but still expect to cut ornaments, tags or 3 mm plywood shapes. Same box, bed and software as the 5W, with roughly twice the engraving speed on wood and real (if slow) cutting up to 5 mm.
editorialDepth.limitations: The 150 × 150 mm bed is the hard limit: no signs, no cutting boards, no batches of more than a few coasters. Build is plastic, Wi-Fi is 2.4 GHz only, and job time estimates ran about 25% short in independent testing.
